summary:
Read every slot; copy each item to the next free position from the left (a write pointer), keeping their order.
When the read is done, everything from the write pointer to the end becomes empty (0). O(n), in place.

question.md:
Slide every item (non-zero) to the left end, keeping their order, so all empty slots (0) end up on the right.

- **Items keep their relative order.**
- **Up to 10⁵ slots**; items can be negative.

think.md:
`[0, 5, 0, 0, 3, 9, 0, 2]` → `[5, 3, 9, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0]`.

The items' final positions are simply 0, 1, 2, … in reading order. So read left to right, writing each item at
the next position; afterwards, the positions not written are the empties.

idea.md: Repeat passes swapping an empty slot with the item to its right, until no swap happens.

lines.text: Pass over the shelf until nothing moves.
An empty slot before an item: swap them, moving the empty one step right.

complexity.md: **Time O(n²):** an item may need many passes to slide left. **Space O(1)** beyond the copy.

steps.text: One pass of swapping empties rightward.
One pass of swapping empties rightward.
One pass of swapping empties rightward.
One pass of swapping empties rightward.
One pass of swapping empties rightward.

walk.title: Bubble each empty slot to the right by swapping it with the item next to it, pass after pass.

limits.md: Each item moves one step per pass. A write pointer puts every item directly in its final slot in a single pass.

approaches.title: Write pointer, then fill with empties

idea.md: Copy each non-zero slot to `a[write++]`. Then set `a[write..n−1]` to 0.

lines.text: Write pointer at the left end.
Items go to the next free slot on the left, in reading order.
Everything after the last item is empty.

steps.text: Read 5: an item, write it at 0.
Read 3: an item, write it at 1.
Read 9: an item, write it at 2.
Read 2: an item, write it at 3.

walk.title: Read every slot; write each item at the next free position on the left. Then fill the rest with empties.

takeaways.md:
- **Move-to-front while keeping order:** write pointer pass, then fill the tail.
- Swapping (`a[write], a[read] = a[read], a[write]`) does both in one pass with the same result.
- Bubble-style approaches are quadratic; write each element once.
